verses.1: On that day, King Ahaziah gave to Queen Esther the house of the Jews. Mordecai came before the king and said what Esther had told him.
verses.2: And the king took away his throne, which he had carried from Haman. He gave it to Mordecai. Esther placed Mordecai in charge of the house of Haman.
verses.3: Ester stood before the king and spoke to him. She knelt down before his feet and pleaded with him to relieve her from the troubles that befell her, as well as from the decisions he had made regarding the Jews.
verses.4: And the king gave Esther the golden necklace. Esther then stood before the king.
verses.5: And he said, “If it is good for the king, and if I find favor in his eyes, and if what I say is right before the king, then I will be considered worthy of being given back those records from the hands of those who have written them down to destroy the Jews throughout all the kingdoms of the king.”
verses.6: For I saw great suffering and destruction when I saw my people suffer. I also saw great destruction and ruin when I saw my homeland destroyed.
verses.7: And Ahash, the king, said to Queen Esther and to Mordecai, the Jew: “I have given Esther the house of Haman. But he shall be hanged on that tree, on the same tree where he tried to harm the Jews.”
verses.8: And you shall write about the Jews in a good manner, in the name of the king. You shall also stamp it with the king’s seal, just as it is written that it should be written in the name of the king and stamped with his seal. It cannot be changed or altered.
verses.9: And the scribes of the king called out at that time, in the third month, which was the month of Sivan, in the year 430. They wrote down everything that Mordecai had commanded them to tell the Jews, as well as the priests and rulers of the provinces from there to Kush, in seventy-two provinces. And they wrote down the names of each province, along with the names of each people.
verses.10: And he wrote it in the name of King Ahššur. He sealed it with the king’s seal. Then he sent scribes to deliver the documents to those who rode on horses, those who were skilled in handling treasures. They were the sons of Ramachi.
verses.11: Which the king gave to the Jews. In every city, they were called upon to stand and fight against those who were trying to destroy and kill all the people and nations of those who were in distress. They took their women and children as captives.
verses.12: On a certain day, in all the kingdoms of King Ahşverosh, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, that is, Adar.
verses.13: The writing of Pashkegan is meant to provide a religion in every country, and it should be accessible to all nations. In the future, the Jews will be able to get rid of their enemies.
verses.14: The horses of the rich and powerful rushed out from their stables, eager to carry out the king’s orders. The law was then given in the temple of the royal palace.
verses.15: And Mordecai went out before the king, wearing a crown of gold, with beautiful jewelry and decorations. The city of Susa was filled with joy and celebration.
verses.16: To the Jews, there was joy, gladness, and celebration.
verses.17: And in every country and city, there will be places where the king’s words and laws bring joy and happiness to the Jews. It will be a good day for them. Many people from other nations will also become Jews, because the fear of the Jews has disappeared from their hearts.
